issues.description: The solution's assembleBookstore function has a different parameter signature than the problem statement and template. The problem and the template indicate a parameterless assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore (commented in the template and described in the problem), but the solution implements private static func assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore while calling assembleBookstore() without arguments. This mismatch (and the internal call/definition mismatch in the solution) will confuse students and prevents straightforward compilation or following the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore function signature consistent across artifacts. Change the solution to declare private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore (remove the 'check: Bool' parameter) so it matches the problem statement and the template comment and the parameterless call in main. Alternatively, if a parameter is required, update the problem statement, template, and the call sites to accept and document the parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an assembleBookstore() function with no parameters, but the solution defines assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore. This introduces an unexpected parameter identifier ('check') in the solution that does not appear in the problem or template, creating a signature and naming mismatch that can confuse students when mapping the requirement to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template by removing the extra parameter. Change the solution signature to: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } so the identifier and signature match the expected assembleBookstore() used in the template and described in the problem statement.
